reviews.author: crivetimihai
reviews.body:
Thank you! I've made some changes and rebased:

prompt_service.py and resource_service.py had the same issue: the PR originally only initialized global_context and context_table inside the PRE_FETCH block, but these variables were used in the POST_FETCH block. If only POST hooks were registered, this would cause UnboundLocalError.

Fix: Moved context initialization before the hook-specific checks:
1. Precompute has_pre_fetch and has_post_fetch
2. Initialize context variables when either hook exists
3. Guard each hook call with its specific flag

commits.message:
fix: Ensure plugin context is initialized before POST hooks

Fix UnboundLocalError when POST_FETCH hooks exist but PRE_FETCH hooks
do not. The global_context and context_table variables must be
initialized before either hook block to ensure they're available for
both PRE and POST hook invocations.

- prompt_service.py: Initialize context variables before hook checks
- resource_service.py: Initialize context variables before hook checks
- Precompute hook existence to avoid redundant checks

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
commits.author: Mihai Criveti

commits.message:
fix: Restore lazy init before has_hooks_for check in resource_service

The has_hooks_for optimization must be called after plugin manager
initialization, not before. Otherwise, uninitialized managers always
return False for hook checks, preventing lazy initialization.

- Move lazy init check before has_hooks_for calls
- Add has_hooks_for method to MockFilterManager in integration test

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
